title: Sixes: Fives and One More
goal: I can find 6 times a number with my 5s and one more group.

card.desc: Bristol knows her 5s, so the 6s become 5 groups plus one more group: 6 × 7 is 35 + 7 = 42. Then she mixes 4s (double, double) and 6s in pictures and word problems, and decides which trick fits each fact.

win: Fives and one more! You know your 6s!

slides.title: On Your Own: Sixes
slides.text: You learned the 6s in class. Now use your 5s on your own. ✋ + ☝️

slides.title: Think about your book
slides.text: Read each question. Tell a grown-up your answer.
prompts: Where does the story happen? Tell one place.
Where would you look for a lost puppy? Why?

items.q: There are 3 rows. Every row has 10 chairs. How many chairs?
items.no: Skip count by 10s, one time for each row.

slides.title: Fives and one more
slides.tip: Add one more group, not one more dot.

slides.title: Shell boxes
slides.text: Marion fills 6 boxes. She puts 9 shells in each box. Make the groups.
slides.hint: Each box is one group. Groups = how many boxes. In each group = shells in one box.

items.why: 5 groups of 9 plus one more group of 9: 45 + 9 = 54.
no: Add one more group of 9, not 1.
6 + 9 adds. 6 × 9 is 6 groups of 9.

slides.title: Which trick?
slides.text: Tap a fact. Is it a 4s fact or a 6s fact?

items.why: Turn it around: 4 × 10. Double 10 is 20. Double 20 is 40.
Turn it around: 4 × 9. Double 9 is 18. Double 18 is 36.

slides.done: 4s: double, double. 6s: 5s plus one more group.

slides.title: Word problems
slides.text: Equal groups? Multiply. Not equal? Add.

items.q: There are 6 vases. Each vase has 4 roses. How many roses?
items.no: Each vase has 4. Use your 5s, then one more group.

items.q: Amy has 6 pens. Ellie has 9 pens. How many pens in all?
items.why: 6 and 9 are not equal groups. Add: 6 + 9 = 15.
items.no: Is there a clue word? Are the groups the same size?

choices: There are 6 bags. Each bag has 5 apples.
no: 6 cats and 5 dogs are not equal groups. That is 6 + 5.
Eating apples is take away: 6 − 5.

items.q: Theo says 6 × 8 = 41. He did 40 + 1. What is 6 × 8 really?
items.no: The extra group has 8 in it, not 1.

sets.no: 3 × 6 is the same as 6 × 3. Start with 5 × 3.

sets.why: 6 groups of 8 is 5 groups of 8 and one more group of 8.
no: Add one more group of 8, not 1.
Each group has 8, so add 8, not 6.

sets.q: There are 6 nests. Each nest has 6 eggs. How many eggs?
sets.no: Each nest has 6. Use your 5s, then one more group.

sets.q: There are 4 tables. Each table has 8 cupcakes. How many cupcakes?
no: 12 is 4 + 8. Each table has 8, so multiply.
16 is only one double. Double again.

sets.q: Liz has 6 stickers. Amy gives her 9 more. How many stickers does Liz have now?
sets.why: 6 and 9 are not equal groups. Add: 6 + 9 = 15.
sets.no: Is there a clue word? Are the groups the same size?

no: 5 × 5 = 25. Add one more group of 5, not 6.
35 is 7 × 5. Start with 5 × 5 = 25.

sets.why: 6 groups of 10 is 5 groups of 10 and one more group of 10.
no: Add one more group of 10, not 1.
Each group has 10, so add 10, not 6.

sets.no: 8 × 6 is the same as 6 × 8. Start with 5 × 8.

sets.q: There are 6 cars. Each car has 4 wheels. How many wheels?
sets.no: Each car has 4. Use your 5s, then one more group.

sets.q: There are 4 plates. Each plate has 9 grapes. How many grapes?
no: 13 is 4 + 9. Each plate has 9, so multiply.
18 is only one double. Double again.

sets.q: Marion has 6 fish. Liz has 8 fish. How many fish in all?
sets.why: 6 and 8 are not equal groups. Add: 6 + 8 = 14.
sets.no: Is there a clue word? Are the groups the same size?

no: 46 is 45 + 1. Add one more group of 9.
Check the ones: 5 + 9 = 14. The answer ends in 4.

sets.no: 9 × 6 is the same as 6 × 9. Start with 5 × 9.

sets.why: 5 groups of 7 plus one more group of 7: 35 + 7 = 42.
no: Add one more group of 7, not 1.
6 + 7 adds. 6 × 7 is 6 groups of 7.

sets.no: 10 × 6 is the same as 6 × 10. Start with 5 × 10.

sets.q: How many stars are in this array?
sets.no: Cover the last row. 5 rows of 5 is 25.

sets.q: There are 6 boxes. Every box has 8 crayons. How many crayons?
sets.no: Every box has 8. Use your 5s, then one more group.

sets.q: There are 4 bags. Every bag has 7 rolls. How many rolls?
no: 11 is 4 + 7. Every bag has 7, so multiply.
14 is only one double. Double again.

sets.q: Ellie has 4 hats. Amy has 6 hats. How many hats in all?
sets.why: 4 and 6 are not equal groups. Add: 4 + 6 = 10.
sets.no: Is there a clue word? Are the groups the same size?

sets.q: Mia says 6 × 3 = 16. What did she do wrong?
choices: She added 1, not one more group of 3.
She added one more group of 5.
sets.why: 5 × 3 = 15. She added 1. She needed one more group of 3: 15 + 3 = 18.
no: One more group of 5 would make 20. That is not 16.
5 × 3 = 15. One more group of 3 is 18, not 16.

practice.intro: Three tries on each one. Only your first try counts. 6s: use your 5s, then add one more group.

questions.q: 6 groups of 10. How many in all?
6 × 9: 5 × 9 = 45. Add one more 9. What do you get?
no: You added 1, not 9.
Check the ones: 5 + 9 = 14. The ones digit is 4.

questions.q: 6 groups of 8. How many in all?

no: Count the groups. There are 6.
The groups are equal. Multiply.

questions.why: Double, double is the trick for 4s.
no: 6s use 5s plus one more group.
You already know 5s. Double, double is for 4s.

questions.q: 6 × 9 and 9 × 6 have the same answer. What is it?
Marion packs 6 boxes. Each box has 7 bones. How many bones?
questions.no: Each box has 7. Use your 5s, then one more box.

questions.q: Ellie has 4 bags. Each bag has 9 apples. How many apples?
Amy saw 6 cats and 7 dogs at the vet. How many animals?
questions.no: Is there a clue word? Are the groups the same size?

questions.q: Theo says 6 × 5 = 26. He did 5 × 5 = 25, then added 1. What is right?
no: The extra group has 5, not 6.
That is Theo's mistake. Add a whole group of 5.

pages.title: Part 1: Fives and one more
pages.directions: Find the 5s fact. Then add one more group.

pages.title: Part 2: Draw it
pages.directions: Draw the groups. Circle 5 groups. Then write the fact.

pages.title: Part 3: 4s and 6s
pages.directions: Write the answer. Use double, double for 4s. Use 5s + one more for 6s.

items.text: 12. There are 6 tanks. Each tank has 5 fish. How many fish?
13. Liz has 6 shells. Marion has 8 shells. How many shells?
14. Amy fills 4 cups. She puts 6 grapes in every cup. How many grapes?

pages.title: Part 5: Book corner
pages.directions: Write one sentence. Use a capital letter and a period.

items.text: 15. Who helps Amy the most? What do they do?

teacher.objective: Bristol learns ×6 as the 5s fact plus one more group (6 × 7 = 35 + 7 = 42), using the 5s she already knows. She then mixes 4s (double, double from Lesson 3) and 6s, picks the right trick for each fact (including turn-arounds like 9 × 6), and keeps choosing multiply or add in word problems.
materials: An index card or sticky note (to cover one group or one row)
Her book, Amy and the Missing Puppy
Printed Lesson 3 and Lesson 4 packets to send home if you can (her task list also tells her to print them)

plan.do: Class slides 1–2. State the goal. Who helps Amy, one clue, what she would do next.
Class slide 3. She says the two doubles out loud before answering. Check last night's after-class score and fix any 4s fact she missed.
Class slides 4–8. Quick 5s round. 6 cups of 4 beans, cover one cup: 20 + 4. Then 6 × 3 with cups, 6 × 7 on the whiteboard array, and Theo's 35 + 1 mistake with the card over a cup of 7.
Class slides 9–11. She says the 5s fact, then "plus one more ___". She builds 6 cups of 6 with beans before the screen. Order the steps for 6 × 9.
Class slides 12–14. Circle the 4 or the 6 on the whiteboard, then the sort (trick and answer before each tap), then read the pictures.
Class slide 15. She reads each one aloud and points to each or says it is missing.
Class slide 16. She writes the trick work for 5 facts on the whiteboard before you click.
Class slide 17. Read the task list together: Tuesday night and Wednesday items. It includes Lesson 3's practice and packet.

watch: Adding 1 instead of one more group (6 × 7 = 36). Point to the covered cup: "How many beans are under the card?"
Adding the wrong group size (6 × 8 = 40 + 6). Ask: "How many are in each group?"
Using the 6s trick on a 4s fact or the other way around. Have her circle the 4 or the 6 first.
Regrouping slips in 45 + 9 and 35 + 7. Let her write it in tens and ones on the whiteboard.

packet_key.answer: Any complete sentence that names a helper and what they do, with a capital letter and a period.

teacher.notes: Show What You Know is at the end of the after-class lesson tonight; a retake gives her a brand-new set of 8. This is the heavy homework night (two nights): Lesson 4 after-class, Lesson 3 practice and packet, Lesson 4 practice and packet page 1. If she scores under 85, start Thursday with 5 minutes of cups and the index card (cover one cup, say the 5s fact, uncover, add the group) before the Prove it lesson. If the 4s slipped, add 3 quick double, double facts too.

tasks: Tuesday night: Do the After-Class Lesson. Finish with Show What You Know.
Tuesday night: Read your book for 15 minutes.
Wednesday: Print and do the Lesson 3 packet (both pages).
Wednesday: Do the Lesson 4 Practice. Try to get 85 or more.
Wednesday: Print the Lesson 4 packet. Do page 1. Save page 2.

Wednesday: Read your book for 15 minutes. Then do the reading lesson Pathways Week 9 Reading: What the Trail Taught Them. Think about what the characters learned. Aim for 85. If it is locked, type 1111.

slides.title: Sixes: Fives and One More
slides.text: You know your 5s. Today they help you with the 6s. ✋ + ☝️

notes.do: Set out: about 60 beans, 6 small cups or paper plates, an index card, whiteboard and marker, her book.
notes.say: Yesterday the 2s helped with the 4s. Today your 5s help with the 6s.
notes.ask: What is the trick for the 4s?
notes.listen: "Double, double." If she cannot say it, do one bean example of 4 × 3 before moving on.

slides.title: Who helps Amy?
slides.text: Think about Amy and the Missing Puppy.
prompts: Who helps Amy the most? What do they do?
What is one clue the girls found?
If you were Amy, what would you do next?
starters: If I were Amy, I would …

notes.do: 5–6 minutes. Tap the gold button for each strong answer.
notes.ask: Who helps Amy the most, and how? What is one clue the girls found? What would you do next as Amy?
notes.listen: A named helper with an action, a specific clue from the book, and a reason for her choice.

items.q: Ellie has 4 boxes. Each box has 7 crayons. How many crayons?
items.why: 4 equal groups of 7. Double 7 is 14, double 14 is 28.

items.q: A picture has 4 rows of 9 stars. How many stars?
no: 32 is 4 × 8. Each row has 9.
13 is 4 + 9. The rows are equal, so multiply.

notes.do: Before she answers, she says the two doubles out loud ("7, 14, 28"). Open last night's after-class score on Formspree and note any missed 4s facts.
notes.listen: 28 and 36. If she gives 14, she stopped after one double: redo it with 4 cups of beans.

slides.title: You know your 5s
slides.text: Count by 5s. These facts will help with the 6s.
slides.tip: The 5s are the base for the 6s. Make them quick!

notes.do: Quick oral round before clicking: say 5 × 3, 5 × 8, 5 × 6, 5 × 9. She answers fast.
notes.ask: What is 5 × 7? How do you know?
notes.listen: Instant 5s. If she has to count from 5 every time, count the 5s together once, touching a finger for each 5.

slides.title: 6 groups = 5 groups + 1 more
slides.text: 6 × 4 means 6 groups of 4.

steps.text: Cover one group. Now you see 5 groups of 4. 5 × 4 = 20. You know that one!
Now add back the one more group. It has 4.

slides.tip: 6 is 5 and 1 more. So ×6 is the 5s fact plus one more group.

notes.do: She makes 6 cups with 4 beans in each. Lay the index card over one cup.
notes.say: 6 groups is 5 groups and 1 more group. Hide one cup. What is left is a 5s fact.
notes.ask: How many cups can you see? How many beans in them? Now lift the card. How many more?
notes.listen: "5 × 4 = 20. Plus 4 more is 24." If she says 21, ask: "How many beans are under the card?"

slides.title: Try 6 × 3
slides.text: Hide one group. Use your 5s. Then add the group back.

notes.do: She builds 6 cups of 3 beans and covers one before she types.
notes.listen: 15, then 18. If she types 16, she added one bean, not one group.

slides.title: Try it with 6 × 7
slides.text: Here are 6 rows of 7 paw prints.
slides.tip: Add one more group, not one more dot. 6 × 7 is 35 + 7, not 35 + 1.

notes.do: On the whiteboard draw 6 rows of 7 dots. She covers the bottom row with the index card.
notes.ask: How many in the top 5 rows? How many in the last row?

slides.title: One more group, not one more bean
slides.text: Theo did 6 × 7 like this: 35 + 1 = 36. ❌

steps.text: The extra group is not 1 bean. It is a whole group of 7.

slides.tip: Ask: how many are in each group? Add that many.

notes.do: Make 6 cups of 7 beans and cover one cup with the card.
notes.say: This is the mistake most kids make. Theo forgot that the hidden cup has 7 beans in it.
notes.ask: How many beans are under the card?

no: You added one dot. Add one more group of 8.
The extra group has 8 in it, not 6.

notes.do: For each fact she says the 5s fact first, then "plus one more ___".
notes.listen: 48, 54, 60. On 45 + 9 watch the regrouping (she may write 44 or 414).

slides.title: Treat bowls
slides.text: Liz sets out 6 bowls. She puts 6 treats in each bowl. Make the groups.
slides.hint: Each bowl is one group. Groups = how many bowls. In each group = treats in one bowl.

notes.do: She builds 6 cups of 6 beans first, then sets the buttons on screen.
notes.ask: Which cup do you hide? What is 5 × 6? What do you add?

slides.title: How to do 6 × 9
slides.text: Tap the steps in the right order.
slides.why: Find the 5s fact, add one more group, then you have the 6s fact.
slides.hint: Start by reading the fact. Next, find the 5s fact. Then add one more group.

notes.ask: Why does "Add one more group of 9" come before 45 + 9?
notes.listen: "First you decide what to add, then you add it."

slides.title: 4s or 6s? Pick the trick
slides.text: Look for the 4 or the 6.
slides.tip: Circle the 4 or the 6 first. Then pick the trick.

notes.do: Write 4 × 8 and 6 × 8 side by side on the whiteboard. She circles the 4 and the 6.
notes.say: Same 8, different trick. The 4 or the 6 tells you which trick.

slides.title: Which trick?
slides.text: Tap a fact. Is it a 4s fact or a 6s fact?

items.why: It has a 4. Double 7 is 14, double 14 is 28.
Turn it around: 4 × 8. Double 8 is 16, double 16 is 32.

slides.done: 4s: double, double. 6s: 5s plus one more group.

notes.do: She says the trick and the answer before she taps each card.
notes.ask: For 8 × 4 and 9 × 6: turn it around. Which number is the 4 or the 6?
notes.listen: She names the trick, not just the answer.

items.why: 6 groups of 5. 5 × 5 = 25, plus one more 5 is 30.
items.no: Count the groups. How many in each group?

no: There are 4 groups, not 8.
The groups are equal. Multiply.

items.no: Cover the last row. 5 rows of 8 is 40.

notes.ask: How many groups? How many in each? Which trick?
notes.listen: 30, 4 × 8, 48. On the array she should cover the bottom row with the card.

slides.title: Word problems
slides.text: Equal groups? Multiply. Not equal? Add.

items.q: Amy's mom has 6 cages. Each cage has 3 bunnies. How many bunnies?
items.no: Each cage has 3. Use your 5s, then one more group.

items.q: There are 4 vans. Each van has 6 dogs. How many dogs?
items.why: 4 equal groups of 6. Double 6 is 12, double 12 is 24.
no: 10 is 4 + 6. Each van has 6, so multiply.
20 is 4 × 5. Each van has 6.

items.q: There are 6 big dogs and 8 small dogs at the park. How many dogs?
items.why: 6 and 8 are not equal groups. Add: 6 + 8 = 14.
items.no: Is there a clue word? Are the groups the same size?

notes.do: She reads each one aloud and points to each (or says it is missing) before answering.
notes.listen: 18, 24, 14. 48 for the park dogs means she multiplied without a clue word.

slides.title: Fact race
slides.text: Write each fact on the whiteboard. Say the trick. Then check.

steps.text: Get your whiteboard and marker. Listen for the first fact.

notes.do: Say a fact. She writes the trick work and the answer on the whiteboard, then you click to check. Do the row twice if time allows; the second time faster.
notes.listen: She writes the work, not only the answer. Note any fact she has to restart.

slides.title: Fives and one more!
slides.text: 6s = the 5s fact plus one more group.
slides.tip: Tonight and Wednesday: check your list. It is a big list, so split it over two days.

notes.do: Open the course page and read the Lesson 4 task list with her. Show which items are for Tuesday night and which are for Wednesday.
notes.say: Thursday is Prove It day: 4s and 6s mixed, hiding numbers, and word problems.
notes.ask: What is the trick for 6s? What do you add?
notes.listen: "5s plus one more group. Add the number in each group."
